s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, ulcerative, purpuric skin lesion with rapid growth and extension
salient_findings: Enlarging purpuric patch on the left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
key_facts: Rapid growth and extension occurred in June 2014
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive, ulcerative, purpuric skin lesion with rapid growth and extension
salient_findings: Enlarging purpuric patch on the left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
key_facts: Rapid growth and extension occurred in June 2014
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors

raw.rationale: The presence of a large, rapidly growing, centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral patches, papules, and macules, along with the histopathological findings of irregular slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31, suggests a malignant process, most consistent with skin cancer.

rejected.label: stroke
rejected.why: no evidence of neurological deficits or vascular events

rejected.label: sun damaged skin
rejected.why: lack of characteristic histopathological features of sun damage

rejected.label: ulcer
rejected.why: while the lesion has ulcerated, the overall clinical and histopathological picture is more consistent with a malignant process than a simple ulcer
